title: Evidence-Gated Allocator instance configuration
description: Safety-bounded operating thresholds. Configuration may make the manager stricter, but cannot waive missing evidence, freshness, mandate or thesis-challenge gates.

minimumExpectedActiveReturn.description: Minimum probability-weighted expected return above the named benchmark for a single-name BUY. Missing inputs do not become zero; they make the gate unresolved.

concentration.description: Caps on the shared loss paths a position weight cannot see. ⚠️ The position axis is not here: the Mandate's maxPositionWeight is that cap, the Kernel refuses a proposal over it, and a second copy under another name only ever told the run two different numbers for one limit. Portfolio heat — total loss if every stop fired at once — is the Mandate's maxDrawdown for the same reason. ⚠️ Every cap here is declared rather than left empty: an absent cap is not "no limit", it is concentration_cap_missing / unevaluated, which is recorded every run and is not a pass. Loosen one by declaring the looser number.

sector.description: Cap on one sector. Declared loose rather than absent — raise it to 0.4 to say "this book is allowed to be a sector bet" and have that be a recorded choice.

theme.description: Cap on one narrative the book is expressing in several names. A theme is declared on the row; an undeclared theme is unevaluated, never zero.

factor.description: Cap on one shared loss path across sectors — the cross-sector complex a sector cap cannot see. Positions declare their factors; an undeclared factor is unevaluated, never zero. ⚠️ A denomination is not a loss path. The currency a holding is quoted in, the venue it lists on and the country of that venue are not shared loss paths, and putting this cap on one of them makes a country allocation decision the Mandate never made — a krw-currency label once stood at 0.31 against this 0.15 and refused every won-denominated name in the market, on a book whose own parked cash had filled the axis. The factor a row declares names what would take several holdings down together; if the label would still be true of a holding that cannot lose money to it, it is not one.

benchmarks.description: The named benchmark each kind of holding is measured against. This methodology is benchmark-relative end to end, so a denominator that changes between runs makes every active return incomparable — including the ones the promotion gate counts. ⚠️ A benchmark has to be denominated in the same currency as the holdings it stands in for, or the difference measures the exchange rate rather than the selection: a KRW-listed S&P 500 ETF against a USD sleeve prices the index and USDKRW at once, and USDKRW moved 1392.20 → 1514.70 → 1359.14 over the twelve months to 2026-09-03 — a band wider than minimumExpectedActiveReturn itself.

koreanEquity.description: KRW-denominated denominator for the KRW sleeve. KODEX 200, listed on XKRX.

usEquity.description: USD-denominated denominator for the XNAS/XNYS sleeve. SPY over IVV and VOO because the denominator is quoted, never held: expense ratio never reaches an active return, and SPY is the one of the three that has a continuous daily close back to 1993-01-29 and the deepest quoted volume of any US-listed equity, so every lens window and every hurdle horizon this manager measures over has a close on both legs.

cashLike.description: KRW-denominated denominator for parked liquidity. KODEX 단기채권, listed on XKRX.

benchmarkHurdleAnnualPct.description: The annualized return the book has to clear to have been worth running rather than held passively. Distinct from minimumExpectedActiveReturn, which is a per-candidate gate: one asks whether this trade is worth doing, the other whether any of it was.

coreDca.description: Broad-ETF deployment is a cash-allocation decision, not a single-name BUY, and is recorded as one.

minimumCashWeightForFirstTranche.description: Cash and short-bond weight required before the first tranche executes. Deploying from a thin cash position turns the reserve into the tranche.

reserveFloorWeight.description: Cash weight that must survive every tranche. A plan whose arithmetic breaches this floor is not a plan, it is a hope about the next deposit.

catchUpMonthlyMaxWeight.description: Ceiling while catching up on a deployment schedule that fell behind. It accelerates placement; it never raises the target.

priceConflictTolerance.description: Relative difference between the vendor price and a web figure that still counts as agreement. Beyond it the vendor reading is selected and the conflict is retained rather than averaged.

experimentalPositionFloor.description: Smallest position, per venue currency, that is worth opening on real money — the amount below which tick size, lot size and the round-trip fee leave no result to measure. ⚠️ It is denominated per venue rather than in the book's base currency because what makes an order unexecutable is a fact about the exchange: the tick, the lot, the price a share trades at and the fee and tax schedule. The base currency is only where the investor keeps score, and one number in it would buy a granular position in a market quoting $0.01 ticks and a three-share position in one quoting 50 KRW ticks on a 33,050 KRW share. Converting into the book's denominator uses the same USDKRW the global NAV already requires. ⚠️ It is an approximation and stays one — exact granularity is a fact about the name, and the sizing operation is given no price.

KRW.description: XKRX. 300,000 KRW is nine to fifteen whole shares across the 20,000–50,000 KRW tick band, so one share is at most about a tenth of the position and one 50 KRW tick is 0.1–0.25% of it. The methodology this is ported from entered KOGAS at 33,050 with ten shares — 330,500 KRW — and called that its Experiment-stage small position.

USD.description: XNAS/XNYS. About one share of a median S&P 500 constituent, and ten or more of a $20 name. Smaller than the Korean floor because US venues quote to $0.01 — 0.005% of a $200 share against 0.15% for a 50 KRW tick on a 33,050 KRW one — so granularity binds far less tightly here. It is not smaller because the sleeve matters less.

releaseBufferMinutes.description: Delay after an exact release/checkpoint time before the at-time WATCH fires.

krCloseBufferMinutes.description: Minutes after the XKRX close before the Korean sleeve's review fires. Reaches nextReviewSequence as buffers.kr. ⚠️ The default was 60 here and 30 in the code until #91, and the code was what ran — nothing passed this key to anything. The behaviour is kept and the declaration corrected to match it, rather than the other way round, because 30/45 is what every document describing this schedule was written against.

usCloseBufferMinutes.description: Minutes after the actual XNYS/XNAS close before the US sleeve's review fires. Reaches nextReviewSequence as buffers.us. Longer than the Korean one, and no note records why — the asymmetry is inherited rather than argued, and is left as it was instead of being flattened on a guess.
